classification.difficultyReason: Requires converting an equal-area condition into a trigonometric equation and using a graph to establish angle bounds.

inlines.text: bisects the area of the sector, show that

spec.description: Unshaded sector with vertex O below horizontal chord AB, curved arc above AB, radius OB labelled r and central angle labelled theta.
spec.mathematics: OA and OB are equal radii. The symmetric orientation is schematic; no numerical angle is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and labels are visible.

answer.worked:
The chord divides the sector into a triangle and a segment of equal area, so the triangle has half the sector's area.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\triangle OAB}&=\frac12r^2\sin\theta\\A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac12r^2\theta\\\frac12r^2\sin\theta&=\frac12\left(\frac12r^2\theta\right)\\\theta&=2\sin\theta.\end{align*}$$
Since $\theta>0$, this equation requires $\sin\theta>0$, hence $0<\theta<\pi$ for the sector angle. Draw $y=\theta$ and $y=2\sin\theta$ on $[0,\pi]$. The sine curve lies above the line for $0<\theta\leq\frac{\pi}{2}$. At $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$, its height is $2>\frac{\pi}{2}$; at $\theta=\pi$, its height is $0<\pi$. Between these angles the sine curve decreases while the line increases, giving their unique nonzero intersection.
Thus $\displaystyle \frac{\pi}{2}<\theta<\pi$.
